text:
matt: FYI — quick follow-up from the encryption-for-weights RFC: I prototyped a streaming, per-layer encryption handshake so loaders can decrypt on the fly without materializing whole shards. Posting notes + tradeoffs.

priya: nice, can you paste the handshake sketch?

matt: high level: manifest.json contains per-shard descriptors plus a sidecar called keys.sidecar which itself is an encrypted blob holding AES keys per layer. Keys.sidecar is encrypted with the customer's KMS-wrapped master key. Runtime does: 1) request ephemeral token from control-plane with least-priv scope, 2) fetch keys.sidecar, 3) unwrap via KMS (or via control-plane proxy), 4) derive per-layer AES-CTR keys and stream-decrypt as chunks are read.

anya: how do we avoid extra round-trips on cold start? fetching full keys.sidecar seems small but still a blocking op for warmup.

matt: good point. keys.sidecar is small (few KB) but KMS unwrap can be ~50-150ms. Proposal: prefetch keys.sidecar during model resolution phase (before routing) and cache ephemeral unwrap result for 30s tied to the node's session. That lets warmup fetch decrypted keys from local cache and start streaming immediately.

zach: what about private/offline deployments where they don't want control-plane involvement?

matt: for Private mode we support direct KMS/HSM plugin and an agent that can unwrap locally. The handshake differs: loader asks local agent for an unwrap token via unix socket instead of control-plane. Same caller flow, just different transport.

priya: eviction and on-disk cache implications? If a layer blob is cached encrypted on disk, decrypting on read is fine, but we can't keep per-layer cleartext on disk. Any guidance?

anya: we could have two modes: decrypt-on-demand (never persist plaintext) and hot-decrypted-cache (in-memory only, evicted according to existing RAM LRU). Team should avoid writing plaintext to local SSD.

matt: agreed. Implementation note: stream-decrypt into pinned GPU buffers when possible, else decrypt into ephemeral memory then memcpy to device. No plaintext file writes.

zach: edge case: what if warmup wants to rehydrate prefix cache across process restarts? With ephemeral unwrap tokens that won't work.

matt: plan: the model manifest can include an optional long-lived escrow token encrypted with customer's KMS that the runtime can persist (encrypted) to disk. On restart the runtime re-requests unwrap via local agent. So disk only stores the encrypted escrow, not plaintext keys. That supports warm restart without control-plane latencies while preserving key protection.

prefetch-bot: deploy-bot: canary of layered-encrypt prototype deployed to canary cluster eng-ml-canary at 2025-02-14T15:40Z :white_check_mark:

priya: operational concerns: telemetry — we need signals for unwrap latency, key-fetch failures, decryption errors, and fallback to unencrypted shards. Make them granular (per model, per shard, per node).

matt: adding to design: emit metrics - key_fetch_ms, kms_unwrap_ms, decrypt_rate_bytes_per_s, decrypt_errors_count. Also emit a boolean label "used_escrow" for warm restarts.

anya: compatibility with existing on-disk safetensors sharding? Will we change byte-layout?

matt: no format change to safetensors payloads. We wrap the existing shard bytes with an encrypted transport layer. The sidecar contains mapping: {shard_id -> [layer_offsets]} so loader can request ranges and decrypt chunk-aligned ranges. That keeps streaming and range-get semantics intact.

zach: how do we handle partial-range reads? CTR mode is good since it's random-access; but we must ensure nonce/IV derivation per layer+chunk to avoid reuse.

priya: propose IV = HMAC(master_layer_key, shard_id || layer_idx || chunk_offset) truncated to 96 bits. Deterministic, safe if master key not reused. Document clearly.

matt: agreed. Add a version byte in sidecar header for IV scheme so we can migrate.

anya: failure modes: If KMS unwrap fails we should fall back to previously-configured fallback model variant (unencrypted) per rollout policy, not auto-serve degraded plaintext.

matt: yes — fallback policy: 1) try local unwrap; 2) if fails and model has unencrypted variant in catalog, route there; 3) otherwise return 5xx with "decryption_failure" and operator alert. No silent plaintext fallback.

priya: security review note: key-sidecar integrity — we need to sign the sidecar (detached signature) to prevent tampering. Control plane will sign when publishing. Loader verifies before unwrap.

zach: signing + KMS unwrap + IV mapping covers integrity and confidentiality. What's the latency budget hit for short chat flows?

matt: with prefetch and unwrap cached on node, zero extra RTT for token exchange. First-start could add ~100-200ms worst-case; can be mitigated with pre-warm jobs. For long-running sessions amortized cost is negligible.

anya: action items: 
- (matt) draft sidecar schema + header version spec (this week)
- (priya) instrument metrics & alerts (key_fetch_ms, decrypt_errors_count) on telemetry board
- (zach) implement local agent socket flow for Private deployments
- (anya) add security review checklist entry for sidecar signature verification and escrow handling

priya: SGTM. Also we should add a short note in the runtime docs about "decrypt-on-demand" vs "hot-decrypted-cache" modes and memory limits.

matt: will do. If nobody objects I'll spin RFC follow-up with schema examples and a minimal wire sample: 

matt: example sidecar header (pseudo):
```
{ "version": 1, "model": "gptx-7b", "shards": [{"id":"s0","layers": [ {"idx":0,"offset":0,"len":123456}, ... ] }], "signature": "base64...", "kms_wrap": "base64..." }
```

priya: can we include a small recovery API for operators to force rotate escrow if keys compromised?

matt: yes, control-plane API: rotate-escrow -> publish new keys.sidecar, mark old as revoked; nodes will fetch refresh on next resolution. We'll add a rollout-safe handshake so active sessions can finish.

anya: ok I'm satisfied. No strong objections from me.

zach: fine by me. Let's get the spec in the RFC follow-up and wire a canary.

matt: thanks everyone — I'll open the follow-up doc and tag you. :thumbsup:
